# Timestamp-imprint policy fixtures

Generated by `crates/pades/oracle/poe_policy_oracle.py` with pinned pyHanko
0.38.1 and pyhanko-certvalidator 0.33.0. This supplemental validation corpus
earns no upstream-function credit. Related original V IDs are recorded in the
manifest; their existing exact tests retain ownership and parameter coverage.

The one freshly signed PAdES PDF has exactly one signature and no document
timestamp. Its target CMS digest and timestamp CMS digest are SHA-256; its
signature timestamp messageImprint is SHA-512 over the authentic target signature
bytes. Signing/genTime is 2020-11-20 and validation is 2029-11-20. Real temporary
loopback Certomancer services supply authentic revocation material. All original
cryptographic/path validation remains active. The revocation policy is the
upstream REQUIRE_REVINFO policy, without soft-fail relaxation.

Eight cases exercise default/explicit-allow policy, permanent imprint denial,
cutoffs in 2019/2025/2030, an independent Provided signature POE control and a
missing-material-POE rejection. Material POEs are exported as exact original
POE digests and dates; only the explicitly named independent control includes
an earlier signature POE. Current HTTP responses are exported separately and
are not asserted to exist in 2020.

The original final Python LTA API accepts all three denied-imprint cases.
Its original `_process_signature_ts` helper performs no POE register call when
the imprint is denied. When allowed explicitly, its positional genTime argument
is interpreted by certvalidator 0.33.0 as poe_type, so actual dt defaults to now.
The manifest records these original observations without changing them.
The native denial tests deliberately enforce a stricter mandatory POE invariant;
they do not claim equivalent final oracle rejection. Independent valid Provided
signature POE remains usable. Without any material POEs Python returns NO_POE
while retaining true API trusted/bottom_line flags; final AdES rejection and
those API flags must not be conflated.

Regenerate a fresh corpus from the V worktree:

```sh
/tmp/pyhanko-oracle/venv/bin/python crates/pades/oracle/poe_policy_oracle.py \
  --output /absolute/fresh/poe-policy
```

`HANKO_POE_POLICY_FIXTURE_DIR` selects a generated corpus for the Rust integration
suite. Scheduled workers require exact directory replication and explicit Cargo
`--config env.HANKO_POE_POLICY_FIXTURE_DIR="..."`; ambient launcher exports are
not proof of native input selection. `common::read_fixture` emits the actual
opened path, SHA-256, host and slot receipt for both manifest and PDF.

After replicating the directory to both workers, use the repository wrapper:

```sh
tools/cargo-locked.sh test -p sigis-pades --test ades_poe_policy \
  --config 'env.HANKO_POE_POLICY_FIXTURE_DIR.value="/absolute/fresh/poe-policy"' \
  --config env.HANKO_POE_POLICY_FIXTURE_DIR.force=true -- --nocapture
```
